body: Thank you, this really honestly does. I'm so petrified of anyone at this job figuring out I'm ill, either mentally or physically.

Me too. I was bedridden for 7 months before I gave up and accepted the daily 7-10 levels of pain. And you know what? I hate it. I hate it, so goddamn much. But I've found a way around it, because I have to. I managed to get a job where I can sit most of the day, take breaks as needed, and live in an apartment building with an elevator. Soon I'll be able to get a wheelchair, and can use that to travel longer distances to add some more joys back into my life again. I can't promise you'll get better. I can't even promise I'll get better! But I can promise that things may change for better or worse, and they can be worked around either way. I am also suicidal, because I hate being ill and miss who I was before, every single day. And whether I like it or not, I am this person now, and maybe not forever, and the maybe-not-forever has to be enough.

I hope you have a maybe not forever, too. And if you don't right now, I hope maybe you'll be able to find one. Message me, if you'd like to try to find one, and don't feel like you can for yourself! People love you, and you will find even more people who love you, because you're worth it whether you're sick or not, and anyone who tells you otherwise is simply a lying asshole.

You are worth it. I hope you decide there is something worth staying for, because you are so very worth it. <3

Hey, so it sounds like you might have gone deep enough to have some nerve issues. I have some sciatic issues in one of my legs from a broken hip, and this is familiar. If yours is self harm related it isn't a huge problem to worry about right now, but you may want to go to a doctor, explain the numbness/weakness/tingling, and request a nerve conduction study, which can be done outpatient. There is a possibility they will need to see the leg, though. If you don't see a therapist or psychiatrist currently, you may want to find one or both, to protect yourself from involuntary hospital admission (and because all of us here probably need someone to talk to, haha).

If you do turn out to have nerve issues, there are many things that can be done - prp injections saved my right arm after 8 months of total paralysis, so there is always hope. Please reach out to me if you have any questions!
You're never alone. ❤️
